surface.entry: deploy/verify-delivery.sh extracts the committed tree with git archive into a temporary directory and runs the real deliverer deploy/dev-up.sh there
surface.isolation: compose.dev.yml now accepts ANTHYS_COMPOSE_PROJECT, ANTHYS_API_PORT and ANTHYS_PG_PORT (defaults anthys-dev, 64700, 64710), so the oracle booted a second stack under a temporary Compose project on 127.0.0.1:64800 and 127.0.0.1:64810 without touching the running dev stack
surface.emptyEnvironment: the archive contained no .env, .secrets, .data, node_modules or dist; deploy/dev-up.sh generated fresh random local secrets in the temporary tree, and the GLM/DingTalk secret files stayed empty, so no provider credential was used
surface.teardown: the oracle runs compose down -v --remove-orphans, removes the temporary image and directory, and the wrapper verified afterwards that the temporary project and image were gone, 64800/64810 were free, and the original anthys-dev stack still ran 4 services on 64700/64710

measurements.comparison: the pre-existing anthys-dev database on 64710 still held 114 migrations during this run, so the fresh stack really applied the full 116-row schema rather than reusing a developer volume

behavior.cleanRoomInstall: From the committed tree alone the delivery script generated local secrets, built the application image, applied all 116 migrations, started postgres, api and worker, and reported live ALIVE and ready READY.
behavior.repeatable: A second identical invocation completed in 36 seconds with exit code 0, ready READY and the migration count unchanged at 116, showing the delivery path is re-runnable without duplicate migration or port/project conflicts.
behavior.noHiddenMachineState: The tree under test was produced by git archive and the oracle asserted the absence of .env, .secrets, .data, node_modules and dist, so developer credentials, dependencies and build output could not satisfy the install.
behavior.cleanup: Teardown removed the temporary Compose project, volumes and image, freed both alternate ports, and left the pre-existing anthys-dev stack running untouched.
